BRAND GUIDELINES

Team Canada
Sentinel

Together, we are a peer.
STRONG · PROUD · FREE · PRIMESTRENGTH.CA
01 — THE IDEA

Strength that protects, not strength that threatens.

Each province alone is a vassal. Together, we are a peer.

Team Canada Sentinel is the visual identity for a single argument: that a divided Canada is weak, and a united Canada is unbreakable. The Sentinel is a guardian, not a conqueror. The bear stands over the land to defend it, with the other animals gathered behind — the polar bear, the black bear, the elk. One country, many kinds, one stand.

Every asset in this system serves unity. The strength is real and it is heavy, but it is always pointed outward at the storm, never inward at our own people. When a Canadian who disagrees with us sees this brand, they should feel invited to stand with us — not warned to get out of the way.

02 — THE MARK

The Shard Maple Leaf.

The primary mark is a maple leaf forged from interlocked geometric shards — a single leaf built from many separate pieces locked together. That is the thesis: the whole is made of parts that only hold their shape because they are joined. At its heart sits a smaller crowned leaf — the sovereign core.

Clear space & minimum size

Give the mark breathing room equal to one crown-point on every side. Never smaller than 32px for digital, 12mm for print. The mark reads on dark first — its default ground is Ink (#16140f) or oxblood. On Paper, use the dark-edge version so the shards keep definition.

03 — THE CHARACTER

The Sentinel.

The Sentinel is the brand's character — an armored guardian bear in Canadian-red shard armor, standing upright over the Canadian shield, the other animals of the nation gathered at its flanks. It is used for emotional, rallying moments: campaign heroes, share images, the close of a long piece. Use it large or not at all; the Sentinel is never a small decoration.

The metal crest — institutional variant

For headers, badges, and formal contexts where the full Sentinel is too much, the forged-steel crest carries the same DNA in a tighter, heraldic form.

04 — COLOR

Oxblood, steel, and paper.

The palette is sampled directly from the artwork. Deep crimsons do the emotional work; steel and gunmetal give weight; Paper and Ink carry all the text. Gold is the single accent — used sparingly, like a seal.

05 — TYPOGRAPHY

Newsreader. Archivo. JetBrains Mono.

A serif that carries warmth and credibility, a heavy sans for force, a mono for data and labels. The same trio as the campaign site, so brand and content feel like one voice.

NEWSREADER · DISPLAY & BODY — editorial, human, the voice
Together, we are a peer.

Used for headlines, pull quotes, and all long-form reading. It is the warmth in the brand.

ARCHIVO · LABELS & FORCE — heavy, structural
STRONG · PROUD · FREE

Eyebrows, tags, banners, calls to action. Always tracked wide in caps.

primestrength.ca · #cdnpoli · 2026

06 — VOICE

The convert, not the crusader.

The brand sounds like a Canadian who did the homework and changed their mind — honest, plain-spoken, unafraid to concede a point, allergic to slogans that insult the reader. It wins by inviting, never by attacking. First person. Concrete. Warm under the strength.

"Each province alone is a vassal. Together, we are a peer."
YES — strength framed as unity. Invites everyone in.
"Unyielding Dominion. Unbreakable. Submit to the Phalanx."
NO — dominance framing. Makes the people we want to win feel like the enemy.
07 — DO & DON'T

Keeping it on-message.

Do

  • Lead with unity — "together," "peer," "one country."
  • Use the Sentinel as a guardian standing over the land.
  • Keep the mark on dark grounds for full shard definition.
  • Let gold be a rare seal, never a fill.
  • Concede the other side's good points before making yours.

Don't

  • Use conquest words: dominion, phalanx, submit, unyielding.
  • Aim the bear's aggression at fellow Canadians.
  • Recolor the mark or place it on busy backgrounds.
  • Stack multiple roaring war-crests in one layout.
  • Use slogans that call the reader stupid for disagreeing.

The system, applied.

Share card (1200×630), profile avatar, and headers all share one frame: oxblood gradient on Ink, shard mark right, Newsreader headline, gold eyebrow and footer.
